title: A good intention counts
hookLine: a sacred hadith: whoever intends a good and doesn't do it, one good is written; whoever does it, ten or more
tomorrow: the duties, or the extras: which one brings you closer?

cards: A week of plans that never happened: the call to an aunt, the form half filled in, the visit pushed to next time. Yesterday's question: you meant to do a good thing and never did; does it count at all?

Hadith thirty-seven is a sacred hadith, words the Prophet, peace be upon him, gives from Allah, reported by Ibn Abbas. And it says yes: whoever intends a good deed and doesn't do it, one full good deed is written.

teach.h: INTEND A GOOD: ONE IS WRITTEN.
teach.b: Here's the whole ledger, in paraphrase from Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim. Intend a good and don't do it: one good deed, written in full.

Intend a good and do it: ten good deeds, up to seven hundred times, and beyond, to many multiples. Intend a bad deed and don't do it: one full good deed. Intend a bad deed and do it: one bad deed, just one.
There's the puzzle. Why would a wrong you never did earn you a good deed? Muslim's wording solves it: because he left it for My sake.
Not doing it wasn't an empty space. Turning away was a choice, and a choice is a deed. So the scale is tilted on purpose.

teach.h: A STOPPED WRONG BECOMES A GOOD.
teach.b: Goods multiply, wrongs stay single, and even a stopped wrong becomes a good.

teach.h: THE SCALE IS TILTED ON PURPOSE.
teach.b: The Qur'an says the first part too, in Pickthall's words: "Whoso bringeth a good deed will receive tenfold the like thereof."
Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: in this ledger, the moment you stop yourself counts as a good thing you did.

how: Muslims often make an intention for a good deed before they're able to do it, trusting this hadith that the intention itself is written, and teachers use it to encourage turning away from a wrong for Allah's sake.

games.q: what does “a good intention counts” mean?
o: a bad thought is written as a sin
a good you set your mind on is already written
only finished deeds go on your record

p: ten, up to seven hundred, and beyond
a bad deed, left for Allah

s: a bad deed you only thought about is written against you as a sin
if you leave it, the hadith says one full good deed is written.
a good deed done can be multiplied far beyond ten
ten, up to seven hundred times, and beyond, to many multiples.
if intending counts, there's no need to actually do the good
meant is one; done is ten and beyond. the hadith tilts toward doing.

games.q: you're about to snap at your sister, and you stop yourself, for God's sake. by hadith thirty-seven, what's written for that moment?
o: nothing: nothing happened, so nothing's written.
a bad deed, because you meant to snap.
a full good deed, for leaving it.
games.why: in Muslim's wording, he left it for My sake, so one full good deed is written. turning away is a deed.

practice: On a scrap of paper, write by hand three small goods you mean to do tomorrow: a call, a dish washed, a kind word to someone specific. Keep them small enough to be real.
For the sit, rest your hand on the list; by this hadith, the meaning is already written.

wordCard.voice: A good intention counts: meant and not done, one good deed is written; meant and done, ten and beyond. And a wrong you turn from becomes a good.

orig.note: Arabic: he intended a good deed. hasanah is a good deed; hamma means he set his mind on it.

carryVoice: Pocket this: intending counts, and the doing of it counts many times over. That's hadith thirty-seven.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 6491; Sahih Muslim 131 (Ibn Abbas: a sacred hadith on intending and doing good and bad deeds); Sahih Muslim 129 (Abu Hurayrah: he left it for My sake)

sources.q: Whoso bringeth a good deed will receive tenfold the like thereof
